does: Cooks food in liquid that is kept just below a boil, so that it turns tender without being knocked about.

intro.what: Simmering keeps food in liquid that moves gently below a rolling boil.
intro.why: It teaches you to judge heat by the movement and sound of the liquid.

how: Bring the liquid up to a boil, then turn the heat down at once.
Find the setting where a few bubbles break the surface now and then.
Leave the lid off or ajar, so that the heat does not build back up to a boil.
Look in from time to time, and top the pot up if food shows above the liquid.

cues.text: A bubble or a small cluster of them rising every moment or so, and a surface that shivers.
Near silence. A pot that rolls and rattles is boiling.

mistakes.mistake: Letting it boil, which toughens meat and turns a stock cloudy.
mistakes.fix: Turn the heat down, or move the pot half off the burner.

mistakes.mistake: Covering the pot tightly, so that it climbs to a boil unseen.

quiz.question: Why keep the liquid at a simmer in this method?
choices: To cook as rapidly as a rolling boil with less noise.
To prevent any liquid from evaporating.
To cook gently without the movement of a rolling boil.
quiz.because: Gentle liquid movement cooks the food without knocking it about as a rolling boil would.

quiz.question: After bringing the liquid to a boil, what comes next?
choices: Turn the heat down at once.
Cover tightly and increase the heat.
Keep the same rolling boil throughout.
quiz.because: Once the liquid reaches a boil, turn the heat down to find a gentle simmer.

quiz.question: Which description matches a simmer?
choices: A rolling surface and a rattling pot.
A shivering surface with a few bubbles now and then.
An almost still surface with no bubbles rising at all.
quiz.because: Occasional bubbles and a shivering surface show a simmer. A rolling, rattling pot is boiling.

quiz.question: A tightly covered pot keeps returning to a boil. What would you change?
choices: Keep it tightly covered and increase the heat.
Stir hard without changing the lid or heat.
Leave the lid off or ajar and lower the heat.
quiz.because: A tight lid can let heat build until the liquid boils. Leave the lid off or ajar and lower the heat.

comes_after.why: A simmer is found by coming down from a boil, so a cook has to know a boil first.
